messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High paging and tail-latency across KV cache nodes. Metric: kv.paging_rate↑ 12x, kv.evictions↑ 9x, p95-gen-latency↑ 450ms. Trigger: continuous-batching window expansion. Link: https://monitoring.redwood/incidents/INC-2410001234 :rotating_light:

emma (eng-oncall): paging spike, multiple customers reporting slow responses (errors + timeouts). Paging looks correlated with a recent batch-window adaptive change we rolled at 03:12 UTC. Paging clusters: us-west-2-a, us-east-1-b.

raj (eng-runtime): seeing lots of KV shard hot-swap & disk IO. Continuous batching backlog grows and KV prefixes are exploding in memory, causing thrash -> paging. Quick check: recent flag `adaptive_batch_window_enabled` toggled true in global scope at 03:12.

maria (eng-sre): alerting incident timeline to oncall-wide. tagging infra. Are we already running any per-tenant overrides?

joel (eng-infra): I can pause the rebalancer but that won't fix the immediate memory pressure. We need to shrink batch window and/or enable stricter prefix eviction. Propose: temporary hotpatch to set `batch_window_ms` to 10 for global, then apply per-customer override for at-risk tenants to 5.

sophie (cust-suc): which customers are impacted? I have a list from support: acme-corp, orb-analytics, and devtools-inc. they're seeing 10-40% error increases. I'll notify them of mitigation plan.

emma (eng-oncall): plan: 1) quick global hotpatch reduce batch_window -> 10ms 2) canary per-tenant override to tenant:acme-corp 3) validate metrics and traces for 5-10m 4) sweep to other tenants if stable 5) revert or keep and make permanent after postmortem. Anyone object? :eyes:

raj (eng-runtime): no objections. I can push hotpatch. Using rctl (internal ops tool) to set flags. Command: ```rctl flag set runtime.batch_window_ms 10 --scope global --reason "mitigate paging storm"```

emma (eng-oncall): do the canary first on a low-traffic shard? prefer shard us-west-2-b where acme-corp shard lives.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime-flag-updater v3.1.2 to config-plane. ETA 30s.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded. change_id: cfg-2410001234-1

raj (eng-runtime): hotpatch applied globally: `runtime.batch_window_ms=10` snapshot cfg-2410001234-1. Rolling out per-tenant override for tenant:acme-corp now: ```rctl flag set runtime.batch_window_ms 5 --scope tenant:acme-corp --reason "canary reduce batch to validate"```

deploy-bot: per-tenant override applied: change_id cfg-2410001234-2

maria (eng-sre): metrics after canary (3m): kv.paging_rate in us-west-2-b down 68%, p95-gen-latency down 220ms. Global still elevated but trending down. No increase in ERROR payloads observed for canary tenant.

emma (eng-oncall): good signal. Sophie please confirm acme-corp is seeing improvement from their side.

sophie (cust-suc): they've confirmed lower error rates and faster responses. Thanks. They asked for ETA on full fix. I'll tell them we'll proceed cautiously with further per-tenant sweeps and follow up with postmortem.

joel (eng-infra): I'll pause the automatic rebalancer to reduce metadata churn: ```infractl rebalancer pause --clusters us-west-2-a,us-east-1-b --until "2026-03-15T05:00:00Z" --reason "incident mitigation"```

raj (eng-runtime): starting tenant sweep: will apply per-tenant overrides to high-impact tenants first (orb-analytics, devtools-inc), then medium ones. Script: ```for t in orb-analytics devtools-inc; do rctl flag set runtime.batch_window_ms 5 --scope tenant:$t --reason "paging mitigation"; done```

deploy-bot: sweep changes applied: cfg-2410001234-3..cfg-2410001234-5

maria (eng-sre): after sweep (8m): global paging_rate down 55%, p95 down 180ms, cpu on cache nodes down 30%. Evictions back to baseline. No significant tail failures reported. Slack alerts flapping reduced.

emma (eng-oncall): reduction looks solid. Next steps: 1) hold for 30m and monitor 2) start small rollback of global hotpatch if safe — prefer keep per-tenant overrides for impacted customers and revert global to previous to avoid underutilization. 3) open incident ticket and assign postmortem.

raj (eng-runtime): I agree. I'll revert global to previous value but keep per-tenant overrides. Command: ```rctl flag set runtime.batch_window_ms 25 --scope global --reason "revert global after mitigation"``` (previous was 25ms)

deploy-bot: global revert applied: cfg-2410001234-6

maria (eng-sre): monitoring 10m after revert: paging stayed low, no regressions. Good.

emma (eng-oncall): handoff: I'll tag night oncall. If anything spikes again, escalate to runtime and infra. Handoff note: we reduced batch_window global -> 10ms then reverted to 25ms while keeping per-tenant overrides at 5ms for 3 impacted tenants. Rebalancer paused in affected clusters. Root cause suspected: adaptive window expansion algorithm overshot under mixed-seq-length workload, causing KV prefix growth and paging.

emma (eng-oncall): ACTIONS: - Create incident in ops (INC-2410001234) with timeline + cfg change IDs. - Postmortem: assign @raj (lead) and @joel (infra) to root cause + fix (algorithm tuning + safety caps). - Customer comms: @sophie to send updates to impacted customers. - Follow-up: add canary tuning (simulate mixed workloads) and automatic guardrail to prevent global adaptive expansion > 15ms without rate-of-change checks.

sophie (cust-suc): I'll draft messages and send now. Signed off by acme-corp rep.

raj (eng-runtime): logging note: saved KV dump and sample traces to s3://incidents/2410001234 for postmortem.

maria (eng-sre): closing incident channel in 30m if stable. Creating ticket and linking grafana/dashboards.

emma (eng-oncall): handing off to night oncall: @night-oncall please take over monitoring. Handoff ts: 2410001876. If paging rate >2x baseline or p95 > +200ms, page oncall.

night-oncall: acknowledged.

emma (eng-oncall): Incident summary saved. Will add timeline and config diffs to incident doc. Thanks team :thumbsup:
